description: A one-in four-out router: a single signal is crossfaded around four outputs by a slider, so that neighbouring outputs overlap as it passes between them

params.text: Moves the signal around the four outputs; at each end only one output carries it, and between two positions both of the outputs it lies between carry part of it
Switched to + the ROUTE CV knob adds the CV input to the slider, switched to - it subtracts it
Attenuates the ROUTE CV input before it is added to the ROUTE slider, 0% to 100%

inputs.text: The signal that is routed to the outputs; unpatched it reads 10V, which turns the module into a four-output voltage source
Moves the routing, 5V peak to peak for the full sweep, added to the ROUTE slider through the ROUTE CV knob

outputs.text: One of the four outputs; it carries the input at whatever share of it the routing gives this output, and silence when the routing is away from it

notes: the input jack is normalled to 10V, so with nothing patched the module puts a moving DC voltage out of its four jacks.
the crossfade never quite reaches unity: each output peaks at about 0.89 of the input, which matches the hardware's crossfader.

inputs.0:
bipolar · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 10V.
inputs.1:
±5V · continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 1V.
